comparator.sourceNotes: The current catalogue (12 May 2026), pp. 6-7 and 28-29, assigns its 75-EC Sustainability major to students who entered in 2025-2026. Their first-year requirements come from the 2025-2026 catalogue, whose p. 6 states a 45-EC core and 60 EC of choice, while pp. 9 and 57-61 identify only eight 5-EC core courses and a zero-credit Personal Development Track. CAP400 in the current catalogue (p. 120) still requires 110 EC including 45 EC of Academic Core. The new 2026 entrants have a 40-EC core and 65 EC of choice, but their major requirements will be set by the 2027-2028 catalogue. Combining that core with the older cohort’s major does not verify one complete pathway. The current catalogue webpage links no corrected edition. MyEUR redirects to institutional sign-in; the public ESSB EER explicitly excludes EUC. This record preserves only the 175 EC supported for the 2025 entrant framework: 40 identified core EC, the current 75-EC major and the stated 60-EC choice allocation. The missing 5 EC are not invented. Sustainability requires Basics of Life; 300-level courses require 60 prior EC. Major choice is 20 EC with at least 10 EC at 300 level; the four selected courses meet that condition. Politics of Public Policy requires SBS208, to be accommodated earlier within choice space. ECB313 cannot overlap MINUC-03. Exchange/off-campus study is limited to 30 EC overall and 15 EC within the major, with approval. The remaining formal credit/cohort questions prevent certification. Second execution: the official 2025–2026 one-page curriculum chart identifies eight core course codes but does not correct their credits or the ARR. The accreditation report publicly deposited in2025 is signed28November2024 and describes the3October2024 assessment, including a10ECBasestone; that historical allocation cannot override the2025 entrant ACC1145EC entry. The60ECchoice space is now unsplit because the catalogue first-year elective counts conflict.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest option now directly responds to the selected interdisciplinary Sustainability major. The two independently evidenced additional LAS directions, society/power/culture and life/mind/health, remain substantively different and feasible. Business/economics is a genuine further direction; the maximum of three is reached without adding a fourth.
